value: chickens (mainly young chicks, but older birds too)

pathogen.value: Salmonella enterica serotype Gallinarum biovar Pullorum

value: passed from hen to egg (vertical transmission)
direct or indirect contact with infected birds
moves between farms through poor biosecurity
sometimes respiratory disease, blindness, or swollen joints

mortality.value: can approach 100% in chicks and poults within the first 2 to 3 weeks after hatching

diagnosis.value: blood/serological testing is used to screen flocks, but a definitive diagnosis needs isolating and identifying the bacteria in the lab

value: routine testing and removal of infected breeding stock
buying birds only from sources known to be free of the disease
biosecurity measures against feed, water, wild birds, rodents, insects and people carrying it in
most US states ban importing poultry unless certified pullorum-free
flock registration and mortality monitoring for breeder flocks (Canada)

treatment_overview.value: treatment is not recommended, because the goal is eliminating the disease from a flock rather than curing infected birds

summary.value: Pullorum disease is a bacterial infection that mainly kills young chicks, often wiping out most of an affected flock in the first weeks of life, and it can also linger in adult birds without obvious signs. It spreads through eggs and contaminated surroundings, so control programs focus on testing and removing infected breeding stock rather than treating sick birds.
